JOS.1.1:
Context of JOS.1.1

“Now after the death of Moses the servant of Yahweh, Yahweh spoke to Joshua the son of Nun, Moses’ servant, saying,”
— JOS.1.1

The Bible emphasises that God’s Word (Greek: Logos) represents the ultimate reason and creative power of God. In the New Testament prologue, John explains that the Word was with God and was God, echoing the creation narrative.

Why this matters:
• God’s light shines in the darkness and cannot be overcome. Jesus brings life and light into a spiritually dark world.
• This light of Christ brings the truth of salvation and eternal life, showing that your existence has meaning and purpose in God’s story.
• Just as God’s first creative act was to bring light into the darkness, no situation is too dark for His light to reach.

Encouragement You Can Apply in Any Life Situation

1. You are not alone — God’s light is present. Just as God’s light pierces darkness, His presence can bring hope into any circumstance.
2. Your life has meaning and purpose — you are part of God’s creative plan.
3. Truth is not unstable — it is founded on Jesus, the Word.
4. No situation is too dark for light to enter — darkness cannot overcome the light.

• God’s light shines in the darkness and cannot be overcome. Jesus brings life and light into a spiritually dark world.
• This light of Christ brings the truth of salvation and eternal life, showing that your existence has meaning and purpose in God’s story.
• Just as God’s first creative act was to bring light into the darkness, no situation is too dark for His light to reach.

Encouragement You Can Apply in Any Life Situation

1. You are not alone — God’s light is present. Just as God’s light pierces darkness, His presence can bring hope into any circumstance.
2. Your life has meaning and purpose — you are part of God’s creative plan.
3. Truth is not unstable — it is founded on Jesus, the Word.
4. No situation is too dark for light to enter — darkness cannot overcome the light.
